The previous ping attempts on both srl1 and srl2 failed with 'Temporary failure in name resolution' even though I was pinging an IP address. This suggests an issue with the `ping` command syntax on SR Linux when `network-instance default` is explicitly specified, possibly causing it to attempt name resolution. I have already verified that both srl1 and srl2 have their ethernet-1/1 interfaces enabled and configured with the correct IP addresses (10.0.12.1/30 and 10.0.12.2/30 respectively). The 'Network is unreachable' error suggests a routing issue, even for a directly connected link. While I previously checked `info from running` which showed the address, it's crucial to ensure the interface and its subinterface are administratively up and the IPv4 configuration is active. I will explicitly check the operational state of the interface ethernet-1/1 and its subinterface 0 on srl1 to confirm it's enabled and has the correct IP address. This will help rule out any discrepancies between the running configuration and the actual operational state.

My previous attempt to set `network-instance default` on `ethernet-1/1.0` directly under the interface context failed. The `show interface ethernet-1/1.0 detail` output confirmed that the subinterface is not associated with any network instance. For a routed interface to be functional, it must be part of a network instance. The correct SR Linux CLI syntax to assign an interface to a network instance is to configure it under the `network-instance` context. I will now apply the command `set network-instance default interface ethernet-1/1.0` on `srl1` to associate the subinterface with the default network instance.
